key_insight: The paper proposes a single framework that connects neural superposition with sparse, interpretable representations. It shows a clear three-step process for finding latent features, separating them, and evaluating how well they are represented.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of understanding and interpreting how neural networks store multiple features in overlapping internal representations, making them hard to analyze and explain.
method: Introduce a unified view of superposition in neural networks as a representational problem.
Use a three-step workflow to identify latent features, disentangle overlapping codes, and assess feature quality.
Provide criteria for comparing how sparse and interpretable the recovered codes are.
impact: This helps AI/ML practitioners move from opaque internal activations toward representations that are easier to inspect, debug, and interpret. It can improve model transparency and support better analysis of what neural networks actually learn.
visual_elements: A left-to-right pipeline showing identify → disentangle → assess
A diagram of overlapping latent features mapped into sparse codes
A comparison chart of dense vs. sparse interpretable representations
An evaluation dashboard with interpretability and disentanglement metrics
paper_title: A unifying framework from neural superposition to sparse interpretable codes
paper_authors: David Klindt, Charles O’Neill, Patrik Reizinger, Harald Maurer, Nina Miolane
